title: Monologue vs Superwhisper Guide 2026
summary: Monologue vs superwhisper compared on accuracy, latency, team features, and compliance to help you choose in October 2026.
body_markdown:
Most voice dictation comparisons treat accuracy and speed as the whole story. In the[Monologue vs superwhisper](https://willowvoice.com/) decision, the more useful questions are about what you actually get back after speaking, and whether the tool can even run on your machine. Those two factors narrow the choice down fast for most people.


**TLDR:**


-


Monologue runs on Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch, and its new mono-1 model now reportedly powers dictation, returning clean, formatted text that fits the app you are in rather than strictly verbatim output.


-


superwhisper runs on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android, offers local processing, and holds SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA certifications, with a self-serve BAA reportedly available for healthcare customers using its cloud models (local-only setups need none).


-


superwhisper now offers enterprise capabilities including centralized billing, SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and admin controls, while Monologue remains individual-only with no team features.


-


In Willow's September 2026 internal benchmark, superwhisper measured roughly 480ms on short dictations, 700ms on average dictations, and 900ms on long ones, while Monologue's mono-1 carries a vendor-published 109ms median latency.


-


A third option covered later in this article runs at ~200ms with 98%+ accuracy, shared custom dictionaries, admin controls, SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance with a signed BAA at the enterprise tier, and a free plan with unlimited dictation for individual evaluation.


**For most professionals, Willow Voice is the stronger choice over both Monologue and superwhisper.** superwhisper already covers Windows and offers a self-serve BAA for healthcare customers on its cloud models, genuine strengths neither Monologue nor Willow Voice can claim outright. But no tool here combines shared custom dictionaries, team leaderboards, consistent ~200ms latency regardless of dictation length, and a signed BAA backed by Enterprise-tier compliance support in a single deployment, the gap that professional and team deployments require.

## What Is Monologue?


Monologue is a voice dictation tool built for writers and creators, living inside the[Every content bundle](https://every.to/) alongside tools like Sparkle, Cora, and Spiral. Speak your thoughts and get clean prose back, a writing companion rather than a raw transcription engine, as covered in more detail in this[Monologue tool comparison](https://willowvoice.com/comparison/monologue) . It's priced at $12/month (billed annually) or $15/month (billed monthly) as a standalone, or $30/month as part of the Every bundle, with a 1,000-word free trial before you commit.


## What Is superwhisper?


[superwhisper](https://superwhisper.com/) is a voice dictation app for Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android built around local model processing, running transcription directly on your device rather than routing audio through the cloud. Model selection is manual, with a range of options from smaller, faster models for lighter hardware to larger models built for higher accuracy on more demanding machines. On iPhone, superwhisper provides a custom keyboard, so dictation works across apps rather than being limited to its own app. It also offers enterprise capabilities such as centralized billing, SAML SSO, and SCIM provisioning, plus AI-powered modes that apply contextual processing to the raw output.


## Monologue vs. superwhisper: Platform Support


Monologue runs on Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch only, which removes it from consideration entirely for Windows users before any other evaluation begins, while superwhisper supports Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android, making it the more practical choice if you work across devices or in a Windows-heavy environment, as detailed in this[willow voice vs superwhisper](https://willowvoice.com/comparison/superwhisper) breakdown.


## Monologue vs. superwhisper: Accuracy


superwhisper's accuracy depends on which model you select and what hardware you're running. Larger models handle complex vocabulary better than smaller ones, forcing a tradeoff between accuracy and usability depending on the device. Domain-specific terms can still require correction cycles even at the highest tier.


Monologue's proprietary model, mono-1, launched September 23, 2026, now powers Monologue dictation. The model formats speech to fit the app you're working in, drawing on surrounding code and app context to handle file names and technical terms, so what you get back is cleaner prose rather than a strict transcript. For writers, that can be a feature. For professionals who need faithful capture of technical terms, it's a structural limitation.


Vendor-published figures for mono-1 show a 109ms median latency and a 7.22% word error rate on WildSpeech-Bench. These are Monologue's own published numbers and have not been independently verified.


## Monologue vs. superwhisper: Speed and Latency


In Willow's September 2026 internal benchmark of consumer dictation tools, superwhisper measured about 480ms on short dictations (1 to 10 seconds), 700ms on average dictations (10 to 60 seconds), and 900ms on long dictations (5+ minutes), with latency growing as dictation length increases. Monologue was not part of this benchmark; its mono-1 model, now live, carries a vendor-published 109ms median latency. Even on short dictations,[superwhisper's larger models](https://willowvoice.com/blog/willow-vs-super-whisper-mac-dictation-2025) trail mono-1's published figure, and the gap widens on longer sessions.


For professionals speaking into a mic throughout the day, latency that grows with dictation length breaks the rhythm of continuous speech, and that delay compounds across a long session, stretching the correction loop. Willow measured 190 to 230ms across short, average, and long dictations in the same benchmark, a figure that holds steady rather than climbing as sessions run longer. Every tool's numbers are in our[full dictation accuracy and speed benchmark](https://willowvoice.com/blog/dictation-accuracy-zero-edit-rate-benchmark) .


## Monologue vs. superwhisper: AI Writing vs. Transcription


Monologue's mono-1 model now powers its dictation, shaping speech into clean, formatted text rather than a literal transcript. It draws on app and screen context, the code file open in an editor or the message you're replying to, to fit output to the destination app.


superwhisper offers both verbatim and AI-assisted modes: users who want a literal transcript can choose that, while AI-powered modes handle contextual processing, formatting, and can use application or screen context to shape output.


The two tools take different approaches to what you get back after speaking. Monologue shapes prose by default, while superwhisper gives you more control over which mode runs.


Both tools now draw on app and screen context, so the real difference comes down to control and defaults: Monologue formats by default, while superwhisper lets you choose the mode for each session.


## Monologue vs. superwhisper: Team and Enterprise Features


Monologue has no team features, no shared configuration, and no compliance certifications. It remains a personal writing tool.


superwhisper's enterprise tier holds SOC 2 Type II certification and is HIPAA compliant, and adds centralized billing, SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and admin controls, so IT teams can manage logins and model choice across a group.


What superwhisper still lacks: shared custom dictionaries and team leaderboards, so vocabulary stays per-user and managers get no adoption data.


## Monologue vs. superwhisper: Privacy and Compliance


Monologue carries no[SOC 2 Type II certification](https://www.aicpa-cima.com/topic/audit-assurance/audit-and-assurance-greater-than-soc-2) or HIPAA certification and publishes no compliance documentation. For anyone in a compliance-sensitive industry, that ends the evaluation early.


superwhisper holds a SOC 2 Type II certification and is HIPAA compliant, and offers a self-serve[Business Associate Agreement](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/privacy/guidance/business-associates/index.html) for healthcare customers using its cloud models. Local-only setups keep audio on device by default and need no BAA at all, an advantage where data residency is non-negotiable. That progress narrows the gap, but team-wide vocabulary and an Enterprise-tier signed BAA with admin-managed rollout remain separate questions.


## Monologue vs. superwhisper: Pricing and Free Tier Access


Monologue offers a 1,000-word free trial, then requires a paid plan at $12/month (billed annually) or $15/month (billed monthly) as a standalone, or $30/month as part of the Every bundle alongside other writing tools.


superwhisper's free tier lets you run local transcription with limited access to its models at no cost, but higher-accuracy models sit behind paid plans. Check superwhisper.com for current pricing before deciding which tier you need for your work.


## Where Monologue Has an Edge


For writers already paying for the Every bundle, Monologue comes at no added cost alongside Spiral and Cora.


Apple Watch support lets you capture quick voice notes from your wrist, a surface superwhisper lacks.


Monologue includes MCP, API, and CLI access alongside its notes, and it offers local models on Mac for piping voice output into automated pipelines.


## Where superwhisper Has an Edge


Windows and Android support alone separate superwhisper from Monologue for a large share of professionals, including developers on Windows workstations and clinical staff at Windows-primary hospital desktops, a distinction worth noting in superwhisper vs otter ai comparisons as well. If your primary machine runs Windows, Monologue is simply not an option.


Local processing is a genuine advantage for privacy-conscious users, with audio staying on device by default and no cloud routing where data residency is non-negotiable. SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA certifications back this up at a compliance level Monologue cannot match, and a self-serve BAA is available for healthcare use on its cloud models.


For individuals in compliance-sensitive industries who need a personal dictation tool on a Mac, superwhisper clears the baseline compliance bar among[dictation software for Mac](https://willowvoice.com/blog/best-voice-dictation-software-mac) options, though this path works only for the individual, with no shared vocabulary and no team leaderboards.


## What Both Tools Leave Unsolved


Monologue publishes no compliance credentials at all. superwhisper holds SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance, offers a self-serve BAA for healthcare customers on its cloud models, and now provides admin controls, centralized billing, SAML SSO, and SCIM provisioning, so account management and model tier settings can be pushed across a group.


What still remains unsolved for both tools is shared vocabulary. Neither offers shared custom dictionaries or team leaderboards, so consistent terminology across a group and adoption visibility for managers are still outside what either product can do. Neither tool pairs shared vocabulary with an Enterprise-tier signed BAA in a single rollout.


## Why Willow Voice Closes These Gaps


The gaps both tools leave aren't obscure edge cases. They're the requirements that surface when dictation moves from personal use to professional teams: consistent latency across mixed hardware, shared vocabulary across a distributed workforce, compliance infrastructure with an executable contract, and full coverage across Windows, Mac, and iOS.


Willow Voice is built around those requirements. A developer speaking a PR description in Cursor on a Windows workstation, a clinician charting on a Mac, a legal professional filing notes on an iPhone, the tool behaves identically across all three, holding ~200ms latency no matter how long the session runs. The context-aware engine reads the active application to handle technical terms, drug names, legal citations, and domain-specific vocabulary, reaching 98%+ accuracy without manual correction cycles. Willow Scribe extends this further, generating complete written content from a spoken prompt instead of capturing speech word-for-word, useful for developers drafting PR descriptions, clinicians summarizing patient encounters, or anyone whose output demand exceeds what raw transcription can handle.


At the team level, shared custom dictionaries standardize terminology org-wide from day one, with no per-user setup. Admin controls push vocabulary changes to every install at once. Team leaderboards give managers adoption visibility without manual tracking. SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance are built into the architecture, with zero data retention and a signed BAA at the Enterprise tier. Individual evaluation starts on a free plan with unlimited dictation and no credit card required.


## FAQs


### Is Monologue better than superwhisper for professional dictation workflows?


Neither tool was built for professional team workflows: Monologue is designed for writers who want polished prose output, while superwhisper targets privacy-focused individuals who prefer local processing. Both fall short on faithful transcription of technical terms, shared team vocabulary, and consistent latency, gaps Willow Voice closes.


### How does superwhisper's accuracy compare to Monologue's accuracy?


superwhisper's accuracy depends on which model you select and what hardware you're running. In Willow Voice's September 2026 internal benchmark, superwhisper measured 480ms on short phrases, 700ms on average, and 900ms on longer passages. Monologue's mono-1 model now powers its dictation and formats the output to match the app you're typing into, so a misread intent means correcting meaning and more than transcription errors.


### When should you choose superwhisper over Monologue?


Choose superwhisper if you're on Windows or Android, since Monologue supports Mac and iOS only, or if local processing and compliance matter, since audio stays on device by default and the tool carries SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance, with a self-serve BAA available for healthcare customers on cloud models. Willow Voice covers Windows, Mac, and iOS with shared dictionaries, team leaderboards, consistent ~200ms latency, and a signed BAA at the Enterprise tier.


## Final Thoughts on Picking the Right Voice Dictation Tool


The[Monologue vs superwhisper](https://willowvoice.com/) decision comes down to your situation. Windows users can choose superwhisper. Writers in the Every bundle can add Monologue at no extra cost. The shared gap is team infrastructure: no shared dictionaries, no admin controls, no team leaderboards. If any of that matters, both fall short, and Willow Voice is built to those specs, with a free plan to evaluate it, no credit card required.
